transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Well, um, what brought me in is... I guess it's what happens some nights after work. Or, you know, after a really tense dinner. I just start eating, and it feels like the decision-making part of me just... shuts off. Like I can literally see myself reaching for more food, but I can't make myself stop. It's so weird, honestly. Kind of like when I'm at work—I'm a cashier, you know, over at the big grocery store on 4th Street. Sometimes I'm scanning items, and my brain just goes on autopilot. Beep, beep, beep. I'll scan a whole cart of groceries and not even remember doing it. The other day, this lady came through my line with, I kid you not, fifty cans of cat food. Fifty! I remember thinking, who even has that many cats? Or maybe it's just one really hungry cat. I had a cat once, growing up. Mr. Whiskers. He used to sleep on top of the refrigerator... but yeah, anyway, the eating thing. It's just like I can't stop myself once I start.

Can you tell me more about those times when you feel like you can't stop eating once you start? Does it feel like a loss of control, where you feel unable to stop or resist the urge to keep eating even if you want to?

Yeah, it's exactly like that. It's like... a total loss of control. I'll just be sitting there, and I know I should stop, I can feel how full I am, but my hands just keep moving. It's like my brain just unplugs. Speaking of unplugging, our registers at work went down for like three hours yesterday. Total nightmare. The manager, Dave—he's this guy who always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts, even in December—he was running around trying to fix the server, but honestly, I don't think he knows the first thing about computers. He was just unplugging things and plugging them back in. We had customers lined up all the way to the frozen food aisle. People get so mad when they have to wait. This one guy actually threw a bag of frozen peas at the conveyor belt. I mean, they're frozen peas, what did he expect that to do? But yeah, the eating... it's like I'm watching myself do it, but I just can't make myself stop, no matter how much I want to.
When you feel like you can't stop eating, do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?

Well, I don't really know if it's uncomfortable, exactly. I mean, I guess I get pretty full, but I haven't really thought about if it hurts or anything. It's hard to tell because I'm just so zoned out. It's kind of like when you're driving home on the same route you take every day, and suddenly you're in your driveway and you don't even remember passing the gas station or the old movie theater. Speaking of the movie theater, they're finally tearing down the one on 5th Avenue. It's been closed for years. I remember seeing Jurassic Park there when I was in college. The seats were so sticky, you know? Like, your shoes would literally peel off the floor when you stood up. They had the best popcorn, though. Real butter, not that weird yellow oil stuff they use now. But anyway, yeah, I don't really know if I get uncomfortably full. I just eat until... I don't know, until the food is gone or I just snap out of it.
Do you find yourself eating much more quickly than normal during these episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating?

I haven't really noticed if I'm eating faster than usual. I guess I'm just not paying attention to the speed of it. It's funny you mention speed, though, because I was just thinking about how fast people drive down my street lately. It's a residential neighborhood, you know? But people just fly by like they're qualifying for the Indy 500. Just yesterday, this kid in a modified Honda Civic came tearing around the corner. The muffler on that thing was so loud it rattled my living room windows. I was trying to watch Jeopardy, and I completely missed the Final Jeopardy clue because of the noise. Ken Jennings is doing a pretty good job hosting, I think, but nobody can really replace Alex Trebek, right? He just had this... presence. But yeah, the eating speed... I really couldn't tell you. I just sort of check out while it's happening.
Do you ever eat alone because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

I don't really know if I eat alone because I'm embarrassed. I mean, I live alone, so I'm usually by myself anyway. It's just me and my cat, Barnaby. He's an orange tabby, huge, like twenty pounds. The vet keeps telling me I need to put him on a diet, but he just meows so pitifully if his bowl is empty. You know how cats are, they act like they haven't been fed in weeks even if they just ate an hour ago. I tried buying that special weight management food, the expensive stuff in the green bag, but he just sniffed it and looked at me like I'd insulted his ancestors. He actually knocked the bowl over on purpose. Cats have so much personality, don't they? My neighbor's dog is the exact opposite, just a big goofy golden retriever who will eat literally anything. I saw him eat a piece of a tennis ball once. But yeah, since I live alone, I'm pretty much always eating by myself, so I haven't really thought about if it's because I'm embarrassed or just because nobody else is around.
Do these episodes where you feel like you can't control your eating cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with things like your work, relationships, or daily life?

Well, I mean, I'm still showing up for my cashier shifts and handling all my responsibilities, so work is mostly fine. Actually, work has been pretty crazy lately because management just installed those new self-checkout machines. People absolutely hate them. This one older guy yesterday spent ten minutes trying to scan the sticker on a bunch of bananas. I had to go over and explain that you have to type in the code for produce. He got so frustrated he just left his whole cart right there and walked out. Can you believe that? Just abandoned a full cart of groceries. 

But anyway, you asked about my daily life and relationships... I guess it does mess with things a bit outside of work. Like, I've started avoiding some family meals lately. Or if I do go, I'm just acting really distracted. My sister always hosts this big Sunday dinner, usually a pot roast or something. She uses our mom's old recipe with the baby carrots and those little red potatoes. You have to use the red ones, because the russet ones get way too mushy in the slow cooker. Mom got that slow cooker as a wedding gift back in the seventies, and my sister still uses it. It works perfectly. They really don't make appliances like they used to, do they? I bought a new toaster at Target and the lever broke after just three months. 

But yeah, I've been making excuses to skip her dinners entirely, or when I'm sitting at the table, I'm just totally spaced out. I can't even focus on the conversation because my head is just spinning. I'm just so worried about what I ate earlier, or thinking about what I'll do to compensate for it all afterward. So I guess it is interfering with that kind of stuff.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah, I do. For the last few months, it's been happening most weeks. I'll have one of those out-of-control eating nights, and then I just... I try to make up for it. I might make myself throw up, or take some laxatives, or just skip meals the next day. Sometimes I'll force myself to go on a really long walk. Speaking of walks, I was out walking Barnaby on his leash the other day—yes, I'm one of those people who walks their cat, he actually loves it—and we saw the weirdest thing. There was this squirrel, right? But it wasn't a normal grey squirrel, it was completely black. I guess it's some kind of genetic mutation or something. I tried to take a picture of it with my phone, but my camera app was acting up again. It keeps freezing every time I try to open it. I think I need to update the software, but honestly, I hate doing those updates because they always move the buttons around and it takes me a week to figure out how to send a text message again. My nephew told me I should just buy a new phone, but they're so expensive now. A thousand dollars for a phone! That's more than my first car cost. It was a '98 Ford Taurus, forest green. The AC never worked, but it got me around. Anyway, yeah, I do try to compensate like that most weeks after those eating episodes.
How often do you have these episodes where you feel like you can't control your eating?

Well, like I was just saying, it's been happening most weeks for the last few months. I'll have one of those nights where I just can't stop eating, and then I have to do something to make up for it, like throwing up or taking laxatives, or skipping meals the next day, or doing that really long walk. It's so exhausting, honestly. Speaking of exhausting, they started doing construction on the street right outside my apartment building. Every morning at 6 AM, it's just this loud drilling noise. *Brrrrrr*. It shakes the whole floor. Barnaby absolutely hates it. He hides under the sofa until they stop around 3 PM. I don't know what they're even fixing. The road looked perfectly fine to me. But you know the city, they always have to dig something up right when you're trying to sleep. I think they're laying down new fiber optic cables or something. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she's convinced it's to install those new 5G towers. She's always reading those conspiracy blogs online. She told me last week that the government is trying to read our thoughts through the WiFi routers. I just nodded and smiled. What else can you do, right? But yeah, the eating thing... most weeks for the last few months.

This supports a diagnosis of bulimia nervosa (F50.20). Binge eating disorder (F50.70) is less likely due to the presence of compensatory behaviors, which are not required for that diagnosis.
